summary.text: Robert Garcia is a Democrat who immigrated from Peru as a child, taught at Long Beach-area colleges and served on the Long Beach City Council (2009–2014) and as mayor of Long Beach (2014–2022). He was first elected to the U.S. House in 2022 and serves on the Oversight and Transportation and Infrastructure committees, where he became the Oversight Committee's ranking member in 2025. He is seeking re-election in the 42nd District.

paragraphs.text: Born in Lima, Peru, in 1977; according to Wikipedia he arrived in the United States with his mother in 1982 at age 5, graduated from Covina High School in 1995, and became a U.S. citizen in his early 20s.

Earned a bachelor's degree in communication studies from California State University, Long Beach (2002), a master's degree in communication management from the University of Southern California (2005), and an Ed.D. in higher education from CSU Long Beach (2010). Wikipedia notes he was Associated Students president at CSU Long Beach.
Worked as a professor of public policy and communications at USC, CSU Long Beach and Long Beach City College; Wikipedia also says he worked as a public information officer at Long Beach City College.
Founded the Long Beach Post, a local news and sports website, in 2007 and sold it before being elected mayor, according to Wikipedia.
Elected to the Long Beach City Council in 2009 and served until 2014, including as vice mayor from 2012 to 2014.
Elected mayor of Long Beach in a June 2014 runoff with 52% of the vote and re-elected in April 2018 with about 80%, serving until 2022, according to Wikipedia.
Won the 42nd District seat in November 2022, defeating Republican John Briscoe 68.4% to 31.6%, and took office January 3, 2023.

In the 119th Congress he serves on the Oversight and Government Reform Committee, where he became ranking member on June 24, 2025, and on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee; Ballotpedia lists his earlier Homeland Security Committee assignment.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 56.5% of the vote to face Republican Brian Burley in the November general election.
